title: The Met Announces New Fall Exhibitions
summary: A sweeping survey of European masterpieces and a dedicated retrospective of contemporary Asian art will headline the upcoming fall season.
content: New York, NY (June 15, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today its highly anticipated fall exhibition lineup. The season will be headlined by two monumental surveys that bridge traditional masterworks and groundbreaking contemporary voices.

The first major exhibition, 'Masters of the European Horizon', will open in October. It features over 150 works borrowed from international collections, offering unprecedented insight into 19th-century trade and artistic exchange.
In November, the Museum will unveil 'Echoes of Tomorrow: Contemporary Asian Perspectives', a sweeping retrospective that highlights the work of 40 living artists from across the Asian diaspora.
The Director of The Met commented: 'We are thrilled to present a fall season that simultaneously honors our historical roots and boldly looks toward the future of global art.'
Both exhibitions will be accompanied by comprehensive catalogues published by The Met and a series of educational programs.

title: Record-Breaking Attendance for Spring Collections
summary: The Museum welcomed over 1.5 million visitors this spring, largely driven by the success of the new Egyptian Wing expansion.
content: New York, NY (May 2, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art has set a new record for spring attendance, welcoming an unprecedented 1.5 million visitors between March and May.

This surge in attendance is largely attributed to the highly successful opening of the recently renovated Egyptian Wing expansion, which features interactive exhibits and newly conserved artifacts never before seen by the public.

'We are deeply moved by the public’s enthusiastic response to our new spaces,' said the Museum's President. 'The Egyptian Wing has always been a beloved cornerstone of The Met, and this expansion allows us to tell a more complete and engaging story of ancient history.'
In addition to the Egyptian Wing, the spring programming featured numerous sold-out lectures and special late-night viewing events.

title: The Costume Institute Spring Gala Date Announced
summary: The highly anticipated annual Gala will take place on the first Monday in May, celebrating the intersection of technology and fashion.
content: New York, NY (April 10, 2026) — The Costume Institute at The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today that the annual Spring Gala will be held on Monday, May 4, 2026.
This year's theme, 'Threads of Tomorrow: Technology and Fashion', explores the intricate and evolving relationship between digital innovation and haute couture.

The Gala will be co-chaired by leading figures in the fashion and technology industries, and will serve as the primary source of funding for The Costume Institute's exhibitions, publications, and capital improvements.
The accompanying exhibition will open to the public on May 7, featuring garments that incorporate smart textiles, 3D printing, and sustainable bio-materials.

title: The Met Acquires Rare Medieval Tapestry
summary: The Cloisters welcomes a magnificent 15th-century Flemish tapestry to its permanent collection.
content: New York, NY (March 22, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art has acquired a breathtaking 15th-century Flemish tapestry, widely considered one of the most significant textile discoveries of the decade.
The tapestry, which depicts an allegorical scene of the changing seasons, will be placed on permanent view at The Met Cloisters starting this summer.
Acquired through the generous support of the Museum's acquisitions fund and private donors, the piece is in remarkably pristine condition, retaining much of its vibrant original dye.

'This acquisition represents a monumental addition to our Medieval collection,' noted the Curator in Charge of Medieval Art. 'Its complex iconography and flawless execution offer a rare window into the artistic achievements of the 1400s.'

title: The Met Appoints New Curator of Modern Art
summary: Dr. Elena Rostova joins The Met to lead the Modern and Contemporary Art department.
content: New York, NY (February 14, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today the appointment of Dr. Elena Rostova as the new lead Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art.
Dr. Rostova brings over two decades of experience, previously serving as the Director of Exhibitions at the global vanguard of contemporary collections.

'We are absolutely thrilled to welcome Elena to our team,' stated the Museum Director. 'Her visionary approach to modern art will help redefine how we present the 20th and 21st centuries to our diverse audience.'

title: Massive Expansion of Digital Archives Launched
summary: Over 500,000 high-resolution images of public domain artworks are now available for unrestricted use.
content: New York, NY (January 30, 2026) — In a monumental step towards global accessibility, The Met has added 500,000 new high-resolution images to its Open Access initiative.
These images cover a vast array of works across all 19 curatorial departments, enabling scholars, artists, and students around the world to study these masterworks closely.
The expansion was funded by a generous grant from the digital preservation society, ensuring the museum's collection remains accessible for future generations.

title: Met Gala Shatters Previous Fundraising Records
summary: The Costume Institute Benefit raised an unprecedented $26 million for the museum.
content: New York, NY (May 6, 2025) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that the annual Costume Institute Benefit, also known as The Met Gala, raised a record-breaking $26 million.
This year's event, themed around sustainability and upcycling in high fashion, saw incredible support from the global fashion and tech industries.
All proceeds will fund the Costume Institute's exhibitions, publications, and acquisitions for the upcoming year.

title: Renovation of European Paintings Galleries Completed
summary: The skylit galleries undergo a massive transformation to better showcase the Museum's masterpieces.
content: New York, NY (April 15, 2025) — Following a three-year renovation project, The Met has officially reopened its European Paintings galleries.
The newly designed spaces feature state-of-the-art climate control, enhanced natural lighting through restored 1930s skylights, and a completely reimagined chronological flow.
Visitors can now experience works by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and Goya in an environment that faithfully replicates the lighting conditions under which they were originally painted.

title: The Met Cloisters Celebrates Its 85th Anniversary
summary: A year-long celebration will honor the history and legacy of the museum's branch dedicated to medieval art.
content: New York, NY (May 10, 2025) — The Met Cloisters, America’s only museum dedicated exclusively to the art and architecture of the Middle Ages, turns 85 this year.
To celebrate, the Museum has planned a series of special performances, lectures, and a temporary exhibition highlighting the original architectural elements transported from Europe in the 1930s.
'The Cloisters remains a sanctuary of peace and historical beauty in the heart of northern Manhattan,' said the curator in charge.

title: Major Acquisition of Contemporary Indigenous Art
summary: The Met acquires 40 new works by contemporary Native American artists.
content: New York, NY (June 2, 2025) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art has significantly expanded its holdings with the acquisition of 40 new works by leading contemporary Indigenous artists.
The collection includes textiles, ceramics, and mixed-media installations that challenge historical narratives and celebrate living traditions.
These works will be integrated into the upcoming American Wing rotation, fostering a dialogue between historic artifacts and modern Indigenous voices.

title: Free Admission for Students All Summer
summary: The Met announces free entry for high school and college students nationwide during the summer months.
content: New York, NY (June 20, 2025) — To encourage young people to engage with art, The Met is offering free admission to all high school and college students across the United States from July 1 through August 31.
This initiative is part of the Museum's broader 'Summer at The Met' program, which includes free outdoor concerts, drawing classes, and guided tours led by teen volunteers.
Students simply need to present a valid student ID at any admissions desk to participate.

title: Hidden Fresco Discovered During Routine Restoration
summary: Conservators uncover a previously unknown 16th-century Italian fresco hidden beneath layers of paint.
content: New York, NY (August 18, 2025) — In a stunning discovery, conservators at The Met have uncovered a hidden 16th-century fresco while restoring a later Baroque canvas.
X-ray and infrared reflectography revealed the underlying composition, which scholars believe may be an early work by a master of the Venetian school.
The museum plans to host a special symposium in the fall to discuss the technical and art-historical implications of the find.

title: Asian Art Department Celebrates Centennial
summary: 100 years of collecting and exhibiting Asian art at The Met is marked by a landmark exhibition.
content: New York, NY (September 5, 2025) — The Department of Asian Art is celebrating its 100th anniversary this year.
To mark the occasion, The Met is opening a landmark exhibition featuring over 200 masterpieces from the collection, many of which have not been on public display for decades.
The centennial celebration will also feature the publication of a comprehensive new catalogue detailing the history of the department's acquisitions.

title: The Met Unveils Comprehensive Sustainability Initiatives
summary: The Museum pledges to reduce its carbon footprint by 50% by the year 2030.
content: New York, NY (October 12, 2025) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced a bold new sustainability plan aimed at halving its carbon emissions by 2030.
The initiative includes transitioning to 100% renewable energy sources, overhauling the building's HVAC systems for maximum efficiency, and eliminating single-use plastics in all dining facilities.
'As stewards of human history, it is our duty to also protect the future of our planet,' stated the museum's leadership.

title: Annual Garden Festival Returns to The Met Cloisters
summary: Celebrate medieval horticulture and botanical heritage with special tours, lectures, and workshops in the Cloister gardens.
content: New York, NY (May 10, 2026) — The Met Cloisters is pleased to announce the return of its annual Garden Festival, celebrating the unique botanical legacy of the Middle Ages. Visitors can enjoy specialized gallery walks and outdoor workshops from June 5 to June 12.
The Cloisters' three gardens—the Judy Black Garden, the Bonnefont Garden, and the Trie Garden—house hundreds of plant species grown in Europe during the medieval period.
This year's festival focus is 'Plants in Medieval Medicine and Myth', exploring how historical remedies and beliefs influenced early botanical illustrations and tapestries.

title: MetPublications Surpasses 1,500 Out-of-Print Titles
summary: The Museum's digital publishing initiative reaches a new milestone, offering free access to historic art publications.
content: New York, NY (April 8, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today that MetPublications, its online portal for art-history publications, has surpassed 1,500 fully digitized, out-of-print books and exhibition catalogues.

Established to make art historical research globally accessible, the platform allows scholars, teachers, and art enthusiasts to read and search classic volumes online or download them as PDFs free of charge.
The latest batch of digitized titles includes landmark catalogues from the 1970s and 1980s, complete with full-resolution plates and historical curatorial essays.

title: The Met Selects Artist for 2026 Facade Commission
summary: Acclaimed sculptor Lauren Halsey chosen to create site-specific works for the Museum's Fifth Avenue niches.
content: New York, NY (March 3, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today that Lauren Halsey has been selected to design the 2026 commission for the Museum's historic facade niches.

Halsey's work will represent the seventh in a series of site-specific commissions for the Fifth Avenue facade, which began in 2019. Her installations will blend classical Egyptian iconography with contemporary urban culture.
The sculptures are scheduled to be unveiled to the public in September 2026 and will remain on view through early 2027.

title: Major Restoration Project Announced for Musical Instruments Wing
summary: Over 50 historic keyboard and string instruments will undergo specialized conservation starting this spring.
content: New York, NY (January 19, 2026) — The Met's Department of Musical Instruments is embarking on a comprehensive, two-year conservation project to restore several of its rarest instruments to playable condition.

The project will focus on Italian spinets, 18th-century English harpsichords, and early American pianofortes, employing non-invasive conservation methodologies to preserve structural integrity while reviving acoustic properties.
Select instruments will be featured in a series of live, intimate gallery concerts and digital recordings once restoration is complete.

title: The Met Appoints New Curator of African Art
summary: Dr. Amara Osei joins to lead the Department of African Art.
content: New York, NY (November 10, 2026) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today the appointment of Dr. Amara Osei.

title: Winter Exhibition: The Golden Age of Spanish Painting
summary: An upcoming exhibition will feature rare loans from the Prado.
content: New York, NY (December 1, 2026) — A comprehensive survey of Spanish Golden Age masters.

title: The Met Announces $50 Million Endowment
summary: A generous gift will fund educational programs for public schools.
content: New York, NY (January 15, 2027) — A transformative $50 million gift from an anonymous donor.

title: Spring Festival of Arts Set for April
summary: The Museum will host a month-long festival featuring live performances.
content: New York, NY (February 20, 2027) — A new Spring Festival of Arts.

title: Major Conservation Grant Awarded
summary: The Met receives funding to restore several large-scale tapestries.
content: New York, NY (March 5, 2027) — The National Endowment for the Humanities awarded a grant.

title: New Interactive Digital Galleries Unveiled
summary: A new wing dedicated to interactive digital art experiences opens.
content: New York, NY (April 12, 2027) — Exploring the intersection of art and technology.

title: Summer Concert Series Lineup Announced
summary: The popular outdoor concert series returns to the rooftop garden.
content: New York, NY (May 15, 2027) — Featuring jazz, classical, and world music.
